casual.en: "Indeed." The question came so abruptly that Liu gave a vague answer, looking toward Sun Sensei as if seeking rescue. Sun Sensei, with a composed face, went on placing stones on the board by himself. He showed no disposition whatever to take part.
casual.ja: 「さやう。」劉は、あまり問が唐突なので、曖昧な返事をしながら、救を求めるやうに、孫先生の方を見た。孫先生は、すまして、独りで、盤面に石を下してゐる。まるで、取り合ふ容子はない。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "You are afflicted with a rare disease. Are you aware of it?" The barbarian monk said this as if to press the point. Hearing of a disease, Liu wore a dubious look, stroking the bamboo wife as he did so—
casual.ja: 「あなたは、珍しい病に罹つて御出になる。それを御存知ですかな。」蛮僧は念を押すやうに、かう云つた。劉は、病と聞いたので、けげんな顔をして、竹婦人を撫でながら、
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "A disease— is it?"
casual.ja: 「病――ですかな。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "It is."
casual.ja: 「さうです。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "No, ever since I was a child . . ." As Liu was about to say something, the barbarian monk cut him off.
casual.ja: 「いや、幼少の時から……」劉が何か云はうとすると、蛮僧はそれを遮つて、
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Drink as you may, you never get drunk, do you?"
casual.ja: 「酒を飲まれても、酔ひますまいな。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: " . . ." Liu stared hard at the other's face and shut his mouth. In fact, drink as he might, this man had never been drunk.
casual.ja: 「……」劉は、ぢろぢろ、相手の顔を見ながら、口を噤んでしまつた。実際この男は、いくら酒を飲んでも、酔つた事がないのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "That is the proof of the disease," the barbarian monk went on with a faint smile. "There is a wine worm in your belly. Unless it is removed, this disease will not be cured. This poor monk has come to cure your disease."
casual.ja: 「それが、病の証拠ですよ。」蛮僧は、うす笑をしながら、語をついで、「腹中に酒虫がゐる。それを除かないと、この病は癒りません。貧道は、あなたの病を癒しに来たのです。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Can it be cured?" Liu let out the words in an uncertain voice before he knew it. And he was ashamed of himself for it.
casual.ja: 「癒りますかな。」劉は思はず覚束なさうな声を出した。さうして、自分でそれを恥ぢた。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "It is because it can be cured that I have come."
casual.ja: 「癒ればこそ、来ましたが。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Then Sun Sensei, who until now had listened in silence to the exchange, suddenly put in a word.
casual.ja: すると、今まで、黙つて、問答を聞いてゐた孫先生が、急に語を挟んだ。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Will you be using some medicine?"
casual.ja: 「何か、薬でも御用ひか。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "No, there will be no need to use anything like medicine," the barbarian monk answered curtly.
casual.ja: 「いや、薬なぞは用ひるまでもありません。」蛮僧は不愛想に、かう答へた。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Sun Sensei, to begin with, despised the two teachings of Dao and Buddha with scarcely any reason. So even when thrown together with a Daoist priest or a monk, he had very rarely exchanged a word. That he should now suddenly feel moved to speak was wholly because the words "wine worm" had caught his interest; fond of wine himself, on hearing this he had grown a little uneasy lest there be a wine worm in his own belly too. When he heard the barbarian monk's grudging answer, however, he suddenly felt as if he had been made a fool of, so with a slight frown he began once more, in silence as before, to place his stones. And at the same time, inwardly, he thought his host Liu a fool for meeting with so insolent a monk.
casual.ja: 孫先生は、元来、道仏の二教を殆、無理由に軽蔑してゐる。だから、道士とか僧侶とかと一しよになつても、口をきいた事は滅多にない。それが、今ふと口を出す気になつたのは、全く酒虫と云ふ語の興味に動かされたからで、酒の好きな先生は、これを聞くと、自分の腹の中にも、酒虫がゐはしないかと、聊、不安になつて来たのである。所が、蛮僧の不承不承な答を聞くと、急に、自分が莫迦にされたやうな気がしたので、先生はちよいと顔をしかめながら、又元の通り、黙々として棋子を下しはじめた。さうして、それと同時に、内心、こんな横柄な坊主に会つたり何ぞする主人の劉を、莫迦げてゐると思ひ出した。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: For his part, Liu of course paid no mind to any such thing.
casual.ja: 劉の方では、勿論そんな事には頓着しない。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Then will you use needles?"
casual.ja: 「では、針でも使ひますかな。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "What, it is a far simpler matter than that."
casual.ja: 「なに、もつと造作のない事です。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Then is it an incantation?"
casual.ja: 「では呪ですかな。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "No, nor is it any incantation."
casual.ja: 「いや、呪でもありません。」
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: After repeating such exchanges, the barbarian monk briefly explained his cure to them. — According to it, he had only to strip naked and lie still in the sun. To Liu this seemed a very easy thing. If he could be cured by that much, there was nothing better than to be cured. Moreover, without himself knowing it, he was a little moved by curiosity at the point of submitting to the barbarian monk's treatment.
casual.ja: かう云ふ会話を繰返した末に、蛮僧は、簡単に、その療法を説明して聞かせた。――それによるに、唯、裸になつて、日向にぢつとしてゐさへすればよいと云ふのである。劉には、それが、甚、容易な事のやうに思はれた。その位の事で癒るなら、癒して貰ふのに越した事はない。その上、意識してはゐなかつたが、蛮僧の治療を受けると云ふ点で、好奇心も少しは動いてゐた。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: So at last Liu was the first to bow his head, and it came to his saying, "Then let me ask you to cure me." — There is such a history behind Liu's lying naked in the threshing-yard in the blazing sun.
casual.ja: そこでとうとう、劉も、こつちから頭を下げて、「では、どうか一つ、癒して頂きませう。」と云ふ事になつた。――劉が、裸で、炎天の打麦場にねころんでゐるのには、かう云ふ謂れが、あるのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Then, telling him not to move, the barbarian monk wound Liu's body round and round with thin cord. Then he bade one of the servants bring an unglazed jar filled with wine to Liu's pillow. That Sun Sensei, good friend of the wine mound, should in the course of things have come to stand witness to this strange cure goes without saying.
casual.ja: すると蛮僧は、身動きをしてはいけないと云ふので、劉の体を細引で、ぐるぐる巻にした。それから、僮僕の一人に云ひつけて、酒を入れた素焼の瓶を一つ、劉の枕もとへ持つて来させた。当座の行きがかりで、糟邱の良友たる孫先生が、この不思議な療治に立合ふ事になつたのは云ふまでもない。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: What sort of thing a wine worm is, what becomes of a man when it is no longer in his belly, what the jar of wine at his pillow is meant for, no one knows but the barbarian monk. Put so, Liu, going out naked into the blazing sun knowing nothing, may seem very heedless, but when ordinary men go through schooling and the like, in truth they are mostly doing much the same thing.
casual.ja: 酒虫と云ふ物が、どんな物だか、それが腹の中にゐなくなると、どうなるのだか、枕もとにある酒の瓶は、何にするつもりなのだか、それを知つてゐるのは、蛮僧の外に一人もない。かう云ふと、何も知らずに、炎天へ裸で出てゐる劉は、甚、迂濶なやうに思はれるが、普通の人間が、学校の教育などをうけるのも、実は大抵、これと同じやうな事をしてゐるのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: III
casual.ja: 三
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Hot. Sweat welled up prickling on his brow, and no sooner had it beaded than it ran lukewarm toward his eyes. As ill luck would have it, he was bound with thin cord, so of course he could not put out a hand to wipe it away. When he tried moving his neck to turn the sweat from its course, he felt at that instant a violent dizziness coming on, so to his regret he gave up that plan too. Meanwhile the sweat unceremoniously wet his eyelids and ran by the side of his nose and round his mouth to under his chin. Exceedingly nasty.
casual.ja: 暑い。額へ汗がぢりぢりと湧いて来て、それが玉になつたかと思ふと、つうつと生暖く、眼の方へ流れて来る。生憎、細引でしばられてゐるから、手を出して拭ふ訳には、勿論行かない。そこで、首を動かして、汗の進路を変へやうとすると、その途端に、はげしく眩暈がしさうな気がしたので、残念ながら、この計画も亦、見合せる事にした。その中に、汗は遠慮なく、眶をぬらして、鼻の側から口許をまはりながら、頤の下まで流れて行く。気味が悪い事夥しい。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Until then he had lain with his eyes open, staring hard at the sky scorched white and the hemp field with its drooping leaves, but once the sweat began to run unchecked he had to give even that up. It was then that Liu learned for the first time that sweat stings when it gets in the eyes. So with the face of a sheep in the slaughterhouse, he meekly shut his eyes and lay baking in the sun, and presently he began to feel a certain pain in the skin of every upturned part of him, face or body alike. Over the whole surface of the skin, forces seemed to be at work pulling in every direction, while the skin itself had not an ounce of elasticity to answer them. Everywhere prickled — that perhaps best describes the pain. This was not the misery of merely sweating. Liu began to find it a little hateful that he had taken the barbarian monk's cure.
casual.ja: それまでは、眼を開いて、白く焦された空や、葉をたらした麻畑を、まじ〳〵と眺めてゐたが、汗が無暗に流れるやうになつてからは、それさへ断念しなければならなくなつた。劉は、この時、始めて、汗が眼にはいると、しみるものだと云ふ事を、知つたのである。そこで、屠所の羊の様な顔をして、神妙に眼をつぶりながら、ぢつと日に照りつけられてゐると、今度は、顔と云はず体と云はず、上になつてゐる部分の皮膚が、次第に或痛みを感じるやうになつて来た。皮膚の全面に、あらゆる方向へ動かうとする力が働いてゐるが、皮膚自身は、それに対して、毫も弾力を持つてゐない。それでどこもかしこも、ぴり〳〵する――とでも説明したら、よからうと思ふ痛みである。これは、汗所の苦しさではない。劉は、少し蛮僧の治療をうけたのが、忌々しくなつて来た。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Yet, to think it over afterwards, this was still the part that was not so hard to bear. — Presently his throat grew thirsty. Liu too knew the story of how Cao Mengde or someone cured his soldiers of thirst by telling them there was a plum grove ahead. But now, however he called to mind the sweet-sour of plums, his thirst was none the less for it. He worked his chin and bit his tongue, but the inside of his mouth still held its heat. Even that would surely have been somewhat easier to bear if it had not been for the unglazed jar at his pillow. From the jar's mouth a rich scent of wine came without interruption, assailing Liu's nose. And, perhaps it was only fancy, but he felt the scent grow stronger with every minute. Thinking at least to look at the jar, Liu opened his eyes. Glancing upward with his eyes alone, all that came in sight were the mouth of the jar and perhaps half of its amply bulging body. That was all that came in sight, but at the same time there rose in Liu's imagining the sight of wine brimming undisturbed in the dim interior of the jar, the colour of gold. Before he knew it he licked his cracked lips all round with his dry tongue, but there was no sign at all of spittle welling up. Even his sweat by now had been dried out of him by the sun, and no longer ran as before.
casual.ja: しかし、これは、後になつて考へて見ると、まだ苦しくない方の部だつたのである。――そのうちに、喉が渇いて来た。劉も、曹孟徳か誰かが、前路に梅林ありと云つて、軍士の渇を医したと云ふ事は知つてゐる。が、今の場合、いくら、梅子の甘酸を念頭に浮べて見ても、喉の渇く事は、少しも前と変りがない。頤を動かして見たり、舌を噛んで見たりしたが、口の中は依然として熱を持つてゐる。それも、枕もとの素焼の瓶がなかつたら、まだ幾分でも、我慢がし易かつたのに違ひない。所が、瓶の口からは、芬々たる酒香が、間断なく、劉の鼻を襲つて来る。しかも、気のせいか、その酒香が、一分毎に、益々高くなつて来るやうな心もちさへする。劉は、せめて、瓶だけでも見ようと思つて、眼をあけた。上眼を使つて見ると、瓶の口と、応揚にふくれた胴の半分ばかりが、眼にはいる。眼にはいるのは、それだけであるが、同時に、劉の想像には、その瓶のうす暗い内部に、黄金のやうな色をした酒のなみ〳〵と湛へてゐる容子が、浮んで来た。思はず、ひびの出来た唇を、乾いた舌で舐めまはして見たが、唾の湧く気色は、更にない。汗さへ今では、日に干されて、前のやうには、流れなくなつてしまつた。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Then a fierce dizziness came on, two or three times running. The headache had not let up since some time before. In his heart Liu resented the barbarian monk more and more. And he thought, too, why a man such as himself should have let himself be talked round by such a fellow into bearing such witless suffering. Meanwhile his throat grew thirstier still. His chest turned strangely queasy. He could no longer bear to lie still. At last, resolved, he opened his panting mouth, meaning to ask the barbarian monk at his pillow to call the cure off. —
casual.ja: すると、はげしい眩暈が、つづいて、二三度起つた。頭痛はさつきから、しつきりなしにしてゐる。劉は、心の中で愈、蛮僧を怨めしく思つた。それから又何故、自分ともあるものが、あんな人間の口車に乗つて、こんな莫迦げた苦しみをするのだらうとも思つた。そのうちに、喉は、益々、渇いて来る。胸は妙にむかついて来る。もう我慢にも、ぢつとしてはゐられない。そこで劉はとう〳〵思切つて、枕もとの蛮僧に、療治の中止を申込むつもりで、喘ぎながら、口を開いた。――
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: At that very instant. Liu began to feel some unnameable lump creeping little by little from his chest up toward his throat. At one moment it seemed to writhe like an earthworm, at another to edge itself along little by little like a gecko. In any case, a soft thing, soft as it was, came squirming and pressing its way up the gullet. And at last, when it had forced its way past below the Adam's apple, it suddenly slipped out of the dark, slimy like a loach or something, and flew outwards with force.
casual.ja: すると、その途端である。劉は、何とも知れない塊が、少しづゝ胸から喉へ這ひ上つて来るのを感じ出した。それが或は蚯蚓のやうに、蠕動してゐるかと思ふと、或は守宮のやうに、少しづゝ居ざつてゐるやうでもある。兎に角或柔い物が、柔いなりに、むづりむづりと、食道を上へせり上つて来るのである。さうしてとうとうしまひに、それが、喉仏の下を、無理にすりぬけたと思ふと、今度はいきなり、鰌か何かのやうにぬるりと暗い所をぬけ出して、勢よく外へとんで出た。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: With that, from the familiar unglazed jar, there came a faint plip, as of something dropping into the wine.
casual.ja: と、その拍子に、例の素焼の瓶の方で、ぽちやりと、何か酒の中へ落ちるやうな音がした。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: At that the barbarian monk suddenly lifted the haunches he had settled and began to undo the thin cord wound about Liu's body. The wine worm was out, he said, so Liu might set his mind at rest.
casual.ja: すると、蛮僧が、急に落ちつけてゐた尻を持ち上げて、劉の体にかゝつてゐる、細引を解きはじめた。もう、酒虫が出たから、安心しろと云ふのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: "Is it out?" Liu said as if groaning, lifting his swimming head, and from mere curiosity, forgetting even his thirst, crawled naked as he was to the side of the jar. At the sight, Sun Sensei too came hurrying toward the two, warding off the sun with his white-feather fan. When all three peered together into the jar, a thing like a small salamander, the colour of its flesh like red mud, was swimming in the wine. It may have been about three sun long. It had a mouth, it had eyes. Somehow, as it swam, it seemed to be drinking the wine. When Liu saw this, his stomach turned suddenly....
casual.ja: 「出ましたかな。」劉は、呻くやうにかう云つて、ふらふらする頭を起しながら、物珍しさの余り、喉の渇いたのも忘れて、裸のまま、瓶の側へ這ひよつた。それと見ると、孫先生も、白羽扇で日をよけながら、急いで、二人の方へやつて来る。さて、三人揃つて瓶の中を覗きこむと、肉の色が朱泥に似た、小さな山椒魚のやうなものが、酒の中を泳いでゐる。長さは、三寸ばかりであらう。口もあれば、眼もある。どうやら、泳ぎながら、酒を飲んでゐるらしい。劉はこれを見ると、急に胸が悪くなつた。……
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: IV
casual.ja: 四
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: The barbarian monk's cure showed itself at once. From that day Liu Dacheng abruptly became unable to drink wine. Now, he says, he dislikes even the smell of it. Yet strangely, from that time Liu's health began little by little to fail. This year makes three years since he spat out the wine worm, and nowhere remains a trace of the round, fat figure of former years. Skin of poor lustre, still oily, wraps the harsh bones of his face, and frost-touched locks linger only faintly above his temples, and there is said to be no counting how many times in the year he now takes to his bed.
casual.ja: 蛮僧の治療の効は、覿面に現れた。劉大成は、その日から、ぱつたり酒が飲めなくなつたのである。今は、匂を嗅ぐのも、嫌だと云ふ。所が、不思議な事に、劉の健康が、それから、少しづつ、衰へて来た。今年で、酒虫を吐いてから、三年になるが、往年の丸丸と肥つてゐた俤は、何処にもない。色光沢の悪い皮膚が、脂じみたまま、険しい顔の骨を包んで、霜に侵された双髩が、纔に、顳顬の上に、残つてゐるばかり、一年の中に、何度、床につくか、わからない位ださうである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: But Liu's health was not the only thing that failed after that. Liu's fortune too has declined with gathering speed, and now the fields by the city wall, counted at three hundred mu, have for the most part passed into other hands. Liu himself, of necessity, has taken a plough in unpractised hands and lives out his wretched days, day by day.
casual.ja: しかし、それ以来、衰へたのは、劉の健康ばかりではない。劉の家産も亦とんとん拍子に傾いて、今では、三百畝を以て数へた負郭の田も、多くは人の手に渡つた。劉自身も、余儀なく、馴れない手に鋤を執つて、佗しいその日その日を送つてゐるのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Since he spat out the wine worm, why did Liu's health fail? Why did his fortune decline — once the spitting of the wine worm and Liu's later ruin are set side by side as cause and effect, this is a question that readily occurs to anyone. Indeed this question has been repeated by people of every occupation living in Changshan, and from their mouths answers of every kind have been given. The three answers given here are in truth no more than the most representative chosen from among them.
casual.ja: 酒虫を吐いて以来、何故、劉の健康が衰へたか。何故、家産が傾いたか――酒虫を吐いたと云ふ事と、劉のその後の零落とを、因果の関係に並べて見る以上、これは、誰にでも起りやすい疑問である。現にこの疑問は、長山に住んでゐる、あらゆる職業の人人によつて繰返され、且、それらの人人の口から、あらゆる種類の答を与へられた。今、ここに挙げる三つの答も、実はその中から、最、代表的なものを選んだのに過ぎない。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: The first answer. The wine worm was Liu's fortune, and not Liu's disease. By chancing to meet an ignorant barbarian monk, he willingly brought about the loss of this heaven-given fortune.
casual.ja: 第一の答。酒虫は、劉の福であつて、劉の病ではない。偶、暗愚の蛮僧に遇つた為に、好んで、この天与の福を失ふやうな事になつたのである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: The second answer. The wine worm was Liu's disease, and not Liu's fortune. For to empty a whole jar at a single drinking is quite beyond what an ordinary man can conceive. Had the wine worm not been removed, Liu must undoubtedly have died before long. Seen in this light, poverty and sickness arriving each in turn should rather be called happiness for Liu.
casual.ja: 第二の答。酒虫は、劉の病であつて、劉の福ではない。何故と云へば、一飲一甕を尽すなどと云ふ事は、到底、常人の考へられない所だからである。そこで、もし酒虫を除かなかつたなら、劉は必久しからずして、死んだのに相違ない。して見ると、貧病、迭に至るのも、寧劉にとつては、幸福と云ふべきである。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: The third answer. The wine worm was neither Liu's disease nor Liu's fortune. Liu from of old did nothing but drink. If wine were taken away from Liu's life, nothing would remain behind. Seen in this light, Liu is the wine worm, and the wine worm is Liu. Hence Liu's casting off the wine worm was the same as killing himself. That is to say, from the day he became unable to drink, Liu is Liu and yet is not Liu. If Liu himself were already gone, then it is entirely natural, and only to be expected, that the health and fortune of the Liu of former days should have been lost.
casual.ja: 第三の答。酒虫は、劉の病でもなければ、劉の福でもない。劉は、昔から酒ばかり飲んでゐた。劉の一生から酒を除けば、後には、何も残らない。して見ると、劉は即酒虫、酒虫は即劉である。だから、劉が酒虫を去つたのは自ら己を殺したのも同前である。つまり、酒が飲めなくなつた日から、劉は劉にして、劉ではない。劉自身が既になくなつてゐたとしたら、昔日の劉の健康なり家産なりが、失はれたのも、至極、当然な話であらう。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: Which of these answers best hits the mark, I myself do not know. I have done no more than list such moral judgements at the end of this tale, in imitation of the *Didacticism* of the Chinese novelists.
casual.ja: これらの答の中で、どれが、最よく、当を得てゐるか、それは自分にもわからない。自分は、唯、支那の小説家の Didacticism に倣つて、かう云ふ道徳的な判断を、この話の最後に、列挙して見たまでゝある。
casual.label: house-checked

casual.en: — Fourth month of the fifth year —
casual.ja: ――五年四月――
casual.label: house-checked

curious.en: I
curious.ja: 一
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: It was a heat such as had not been known for years. Wherever one looked, the roof-tiles of the houses, set hard with mud, threw back the sunlight dully, like lead, and even the swallows' nests hung beneath them seemed, at this rate, likely to steam the chicks and eggs inside them alive where they lay. Still more, every field that was a field, whether hemp or millet, hung its head limply in the reek of the earth, and there was not one thing that, green as it was, was not wilted. The sky seen above those fields, perhaps stricken with the closeness of these past days, though fair, hung thick and turbid in the air near the ground, and here and there mere shapes of towering cloud, like hail parched in a roasting pan, floated in lumps. — The tale of the "wine worm" begins with three men who have gone out of their way into the threshing-yard in the blazing sun in such weather.
curious.ja: 近年にない暑さである。どこを見ても、泥で固めた家々の屋根瓦が、鉛のやうに鈍く日の光を反射して、その下に懸けてある燕の巣さへ、この塩梅では中にゐる雛や卵を、そのまゝ蒸殺してしまふかと思はれる。まして、畑と云ふ畑は、麻でも黍でも、皆、土いきれにぐつたりと頭をさげて、何一つ、青いなりに、萎れてゐないものはない。その畑の上に見える空も、この頃の温気に中てられたせいか、地上に近い大気は、晴れながら、どんよりと濁つて、その所々に、霰を炮烙で煎つたやうな、形ばかりの雲の峰が、つぶつぶと浮かんでゐる。――「酒虫」の話は、この陽気に、わざ〳〵炎天の打麦場へ出てゐる、三人の男で始まるのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Strangely, one of them lay naked, on his back upon the bare ground. What was more, for some reason, his hands and his feet were wound round and round with thin cord. Yet the man himself showed no particular sign of minding it. He was a short man, of good colour, somehow giving a sense of dull heaviness, fat as a pig. Then a handy unglazed jar stood at this man's pillow, but what was inside that, too, was not to be known.
curious.ja: 不思議な事に、その中の一人は、素裸で、仰向けに地面へ寝ころんでゐる。おまけに、どう云ふ訳だか、細引で、手も足もぐる〳〵巻にされてゐる。が格別当人は、それを苦に病んでゐる容子もない。背の低い、血色の好い、どことなく鈍重と云ふ感じを起させる、豚のやうに肥つた男である。それから手ごろな素焼の瓶が一つ、この男の枕もとに置いてあるが、これも中に何がはいつてゐるのだか、わからない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Another was a monk in a yellow robe, with a small bronze ring hung from his ear, of a strangely antique visage at first sight. His skin was dark beyond the common, and, to see the curl of his hair and beard, he seemed a man come from somewhere west of the Congling. For some time he had been patiently waving a red-handled fly-whisk to drive off the horseflies and flies that would fasten upon the naked man, but, grown a little tired at last, as it seemed, he had now come beside that same unglazed jar and squatted there with pompous self-importance, like a turkey.
curious.ja: もう一人は、黄色い法衣を着て、耳に小さな青銅の環をさげた、一見、象貌の奇古な沙門である。皮膚の色が並はづれて黒い上に、髪や鬚の縮れてゐる所を見ると、どうも葱嶺の西からでも来た人間らしい。これはさつきから根気よく、朱柄の麈尾をふりふり、裸の男にたからうとする虻や蠅を追つてゐたが、流石に少しくたびれたと見えて、今では、例の素焼の瓶の側へ来て、七面鳥のやうな恰好をしながら、勿体らしくしやがんでゐる。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: The Congling, the Onion Range, is the mountains west of China. To come from beyond them is to come from Central Asia, far outside China.

curious.en: The last stood far apart from the other two, under the eaves of a thatched hut in the corner of the threshing-yard. This man grew on the tip of his chin, as a mere token, a beard like a rat's tail, and his get-up was a black-cloth gown long enough to hide his heels, with a tea-brown sash whose knot hung slack. From the careful way he plied from time to time a fan made of white birds' feathers, he was probably a Confucian scholar or something of the sort.
curious.ja: あとの一人は、この二人からずつと離れて、打麦場の隅にある草房の軒下に立つてゐる。この男は、頤の先に、鼠の尻尾のやうな髯を、申訳だけに生やして、踵が隠れる程長い皁布衫に、結目をだらしなく垂らした茶褐帯と云ふ拵へである。白い鳥の羽で製つた団扇を、時々大事さうに使つてゐる容子では、多分、儒者か何かにちがひない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: All three alike kept their mouths shut as if by agreement. Nor did they so much as stir, as though they took some uncommon interest in whatever was about to happen, and for that held their breath.
curious.ja: この三人が三人とも、云ひ合せたやうに、口を噤んでゐる。その上、碌に身動きさへもしない、何か、これから起らうとする事に、非常な興味でも持つてゐて、その為に、皆、息をひそめてゐるのではないかと思はれる。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: It must have been exactly noon. The dogs too, perhaps sunk in their midday doze, were not heard to bark once. The hemp and millet ringing the threshing-yard shone their green leaves in the sun and stood hushed and perfectly still. And the sky seen beyond them, all stifling heat, trailed a shimmering haze, so that one might have doubted whether even the towering clouds were panting in this drought. Look where one would, nothing seemed to breathe but these three men. And those three kept their silence like the clay images enshrined in the Guandi Temple. . . .
curious.ja: 日は正に、亭午であらう。犬も午睡をしてゐるせいか、吠える声一つ聞えない。打麦場を囲んでゐる麻や黍も、青い葉を日に光らせて、ひつそりかんと静まつてゐる。それから、その末に見える空も、一面に、熱くるしく、炎靄をたゞよはせて、雲の峰さへもこの旱に、肩息をついてゐるのかと、疑はれる。見渡した所、息が通つてゐるらしいのは、この三人の男の外にない。さうして、その三人が又、関帝廟に安置してある、泥塑の像のやうに沈黙を守つてゐる。……
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Of course, this is no tale of Japan. — It is what happened one summer on the threshing-yard of the Liu family at a place called Changshan in China.
curious.ja: 勿論、日本の話ではない。――支那の長山と云ふ所にある劉氏の打麦場で、或年の夏、起つた出来事である。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: II
curious.ja: 二
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The man lying naked in the blazing sun was the master of this threshing-yard, surnamed Liu and named Dacheng, one of the leading men of fortune in Changshan. This man's one indulgence was drink, and from morning on he was scarcely ever parted from the cup. And that, "whenever he drank alone, he finished a whole jar," was a capacity beyond ordinary men. Though, as already said, "three hundred mu of fields by the city wall, half planted with millet," so there was not the least fear that drink would burden his estate.
curious.ja: 裸で、炎天に寝ころんでゐるのは、この打麦場の主人で、姓は劉、名は大成と云ふ、長山では、屈指の素封家の一人である。この男の道楽は、酒を飲む一方で、朝から、殆、盃を離したと云ふ事がない。それも、「独酌する毎に輒、一甕を尽す」と云ふのだから、人並をはづれた酒量である。尤も前にも云つたやうに、「負郭の田三百畝、半は黍を種う」と云ふので、飲の為に家産が累はされるやうな惧は、万々ない。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: A mu is a Chinese measure of field area. Three hundred mu means a large landed estate.
notes.span: three hundred mu of fields by the city wall

curious.en: Why he should be lying naked in the blazing sun has a history behind it, as follows. — That day, as Liu, together with Sun Sensei, his fellow drinker (this is the scholar who had held the white-feather fan), was fighting out a game on the board, leaning against the bamboo wife in a well-aired room, the maidservant came and said, "A monk, lodging they say at Hodoji or somewhere, has just come and insists upon seeing the master. What shall I do?"
curious.ja: それが、何故、裸で、炎天に寝ころんでゐるかと云ふと、それには、かう云ふ因縁がある。――その日、劉が、同じ飲仲間の孫先生と一しよに（これが、白羽扇を持つてゐた儒者である。）風通しのいゝ室で、竹婦人に靠れながら、棋局を闘はせてゐると、召使ひの丫鬟が来て、「唯今、宝幢寺とかにゐると云ふ、坊さんが御見えになりまして、是非、御主人に御目にかゝりたいと申しますが、いかゞ致しませう。」と云ふ。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: A hollow bolster of woven bamboo, leaned against for coolness in summer heat.

curious.en: "What, Hodoji?" So saying, Liu blinked his small eyes as if dazzled, and then, heaving up his fat body, hot-looking in itself, ordered, "Then show him in here." Then, with a glance at Sun Sensei's face, he added, "It must be that monk, I suppose."
curious.ja: 「なに、宝幢寺？」かう云つて、劉は小さな眼を、まぶしさうに、しばたたいたが、やがて、暑さうに肥つた体を起しながら、「では、こゝへ御通し申せ。」と云ひつけた。それから、孫先生の顔をちよいと見て「大方あの坊主でせう。」とつけ加へた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The monk lodging at Hodoji was a barbarian monk come from the Western Regions. As he both practised medicine and administered the arts of the bedchamber, his repute stood high in these parts. For instance, rumours all but miraculous were going round in full force, that Zhang San's black cataract had suddenly taken a turn for the better, that Li Si's byouen had been healed on the spot. — Both men had heard these rumours. With what business could that barbarian monk now have gone out of his way to come to Liu's house? Of course Liu had no recollection at all of having sent to fetch him.
curious.ja: 宝幢寺にゐる坊主と云ふのは、西域から来た蛮僧である。これが、医療も加へれば、房術も施すと云ふので、この界隈では、評判が高い。たとへば、張三の黒内障が、忽、快方に向つたとか、李四の病閹が、即座に平癒したとか、殆、奇蹟に近い噂が盛に行はれてゐるのである。――この噂は、二人とも聞いてゐた。その蛮僧が、今、何の用で、わざわざ、劉の所へ出むいて来たのであらう。勿論、劉の方から、迎へにやつた覚えなどは、全然ない。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: An obscure ailment of the private parts. The original names it without explaining it.

curious.en: Let it be said in passing that Liu was not, by nature, a man who delighted in visitors. But when he already had one guest with him, and a new visitor came, he would generally receive him readily enough. He had what might be called a childish vanity, as if to boast before his guest of having guests. Besides, today's barbarian monk was just now talked of wherever one went. By no means a visitor to be ashamed of meeting. — Liu's motive in proposing to meet him lay much in this direction.
curious.ja: 序に云つて置くが、劉は、一体、来客を悦ぶやうな男ではない。が、他に一人、来客がある場合に、新来の客が来たとなると、大抵ならば、快く会つてやる。客の手前、客のあるのを自慢するとでも云つたらよささうな、小供らしい虚栄心を持つてゐるからである。それに、今日の蛮僧は、この頃、どこででも評判になつてゐる。決して、会つて恥しいやうな客ではない。――劉が会はうと云ひ出した動機は、大体こんな所にあつたのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "What can his business be?"
curious.ja: 「何の用でせう。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Begging, most likely. He will be asking us to bestow some alms, I suppose."
curious.ja: 「まづ、物貰ひですな。信施でもしてくれと云ふのでせう。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: While the two were talking such matters over, presently there entered, led by the maidservant, as they looked, a strange-formed monk, tall and with eyes like faceted amethyst. He wore a yellow robe, his grown-out curling hair hanging heavily, as if a nuisance, over his shoulders. Fly-whisk with its red handle in hand, he planted himself heavily in the middle of the room. He offered no greeting and said not a word.
curious.ja: こんな事を、二人で話してゐる内に、やがて、丫鬟の案内で、はいつて来たのを見ると、背の高い、紫石稜のやうな眼をした、異形な沙門である。黄色い法衣を着て、その肩に、縮れた髪の伸びたのを、うるささうに垂らしてゐる。それが、朱柄の麈尾を持つたまゝ、のつそり室のまん中に立つた。挨拶もしなければ、口もきかない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Liu hung back for a while, but as the silence grew somehow uneasy, he ventured, "Have you some business with me?"
curious.ja: 劉は、しばらく、ためらつてゐたが、その内に、それが何となく、不安になつて来たので「何か御用かな。」と訊いて見た。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: At which the barbarian monk said, "You are the one, are you not, who is fond of drink."
curious.ja: すると、蛮僧が云つた。「あなたでせうな、酒が好きなのは。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Indeed." The question came so abruptly that Liu gave a vague answer, looking toward Sun Sensei as if seeking rescue. Sun Sensei, with a composed face, went on placing stones on the board by himself. He showed no disposition whatever to take part.
curious.ja: 「さやう。」劉は、あまり問が唐突なので、曖昧な返事をしながら、救を求めるやうに、孫先生の方を見た。孫先生は、すまして、独りで、盤面に石を下してゐる。まるで、取り合ふ容子はない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "You are afflicted with a rare disease. Are you aware of it?" The barbarian monk said this as if to press the point. Hearing of a disease, Liu wore a dubious look, stroking the bamboo wife as he did so—
curious.ja: 「あなたは、珍しい病に罹つて御出になる。それを御存知ですかな。」蛮僧は念を押すやうに、かう云つた。劉は、病と聞いたので、けげんな顔をして、竹婦人を撫でながら、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "A disease— is it?"
curious.ja: 「病――ですかな。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "It is."
curious.ja: 「さうです。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "No, ever since I was a child . . ." As Liu was about to say something, the barbarian monk cut him off.
curious.ja: 「いや、幼少の時から……」劉が何か云はうとすると、蛮僧はそれを遮つて、
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Drink as you may, you never get drunk, do you?"
curious.ja: 「酒を飲まれても、酔ひますまいな。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: " . . ." Liu stared hard at the other's face and shut his mouth. In fact, drink as he might, this man had never been drunk.
curious.ja: 「……」劉は、ぢろぢろ、相手の顔を見ながら、口を噤んでしまつた。実際この男は、いくら酒を飲んでも、酔つた事がないのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "That is the proof of the disease," the barbarian monk went on with a faint smile. "There is a wine worm in your belly. Unless it is removed, this disease will not be cured. This poor monk has come to cure your disease."
curious.ja: 「それが、病の証拠ですよ。」蛮僧は、うす笑をしながら、語をついで、「腹中に酒虫がゐる。それを除かないと、この病は癒りません。貧道は、あなたの病を癒しに来たのです。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Can it be cured?" Liu let out the words in an uncertain voice before he knew it. And he was ashamed of himself for it.
curious.ja: 「癒りますかな。」劉は思はず覚束なさうな声を出した。さうして、自分でそれを恥ぢた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "It is because it can be cured that I have come."
curious.ja: 「癒ればこそ、来ましたが。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Then Sun Sensei, who until now had listened in silence to the exchange, suddenly put in a word.
curious.ja: すると、今まで、黙つて、問答を聞いてゐた孫先生が、急に語を挟んだ。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Will you be using some medicine?"
curious.ja: 「何か、薬でも御用ひか。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "No, there will be no need to use anything like medicine," the barbarian monk answered curtly.
curious.ja: 「いや、薬なぞは用ひるまでもありません。」蛮僧は不愛想に、かう答へた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Sun Sensei, to begin with, despised the two teachings of Dao and Buddha with scarcely any reason. So even when thrown together with a Daoist priest or a monk, he had very rarely exchanged a word. That he should now suddenly feel moved to speak was wholly because the words "wine worm" had caught his interest; fond of wine himself, on hearing this he had grown a little uneasy lest there be a wine worm in his own belly too. When he heard the barbarian monk's grudging answer, however, he suddenly felt as if he had been made a fool of, so with a slight frown he began once more, in silence as before, to place his stones. And at the same time, inwardly, he thought his host Liu a fool for meeting with so insolent a monk.
curious.ja: 孫先生は、元来、道仏の二教を殆、無理由に軽蔑してゐる。だから、道士とか僧侶とかと一しよになつても、口をきいた事は滅多にない。それが、今ふと口を出す気になつたのは、全く酒虫と云ふ語の興味に動かされたからで、酒の好きな先生は、これを聞くと、自分の腹の中にも、酒虫がゐはしないかと、聊、不安になつて来たのである。所が、蛮僧の不承不承な答を聞くと、急に、自分が莫迦にされたやうな気がしたので、先生はちよいと顔をしかめながら、又元の通り、黙々として棋子を下しはじめた。さうして、それと同時に、内心、こんな横柄な坊主に会つたり何ぞする主人の劉を、莫迦げてゐると思ひ出した。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: For his part, Liu of course paid no mind to any such thing.
curious.ja: 劉の方では、勿論そんな事には頓着しない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Then will you use needles?"
curious.ja: 「では、針でも使ひますかな。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "What, it is a far simpler matter than that."
curious.ja: 「なに、もつと造作のない事です。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Then is it an incantation?"
curious.ja: 「では呪ですかな。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "No, nor is it any incantation."
curious.ja: 「いや、呪でもありません。」
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: After repeating such exchanges, the barbarian monk briefly explained his cure to them. — According to it, he had only to strip naked and lie still in the sun. To Liu this seemed a very easy thing. If he could be cured by that much, there was nothing better than to be cured. Moreover, without himself knowing it, he was a little moved by curiosity at the point of submitting to the barbarian monk's treatment.
curious.ja: かう云ふ会話を繰返した末に、蛮僧は、簡単に、その療法を説明して聞かせた。――それによるに、唯、裸になつて、日向にぢつとしてゐさへすればよいと云ふのである。劉には、それが、甚、容易な事のやうに思はれた。その位の事で癒るなら、癒して貰ふのに越した事はない。その上、意識してはゐなかつたが、蛮僧の治療を受けると云ふ点で、好奇心も少しは動いてゐた。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: So at last Liu was the first to bow his head, and it came to his saying, "Then let me ask you to cure me." — There is such a history behind Liu's lying naked in the threshing-yard in the blazing sun.
curious.ja: そこでとうとう、劉も、こつちから頭を下げて、「では、どうか一つ、癒して頂きませう。」と云ふ事になつた。――劉が、裸で、炎天の打麦場にねころんでゐるのには、かう云ふ謂れが、あるのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Then, telling him not to move, the barbarian monk wound Liu's body round and round with thin cord. Then he bade one of the servants bring an unglazed jar filled with wine to Liu's pillow. That Sun Sensei, good friend of the wine mound, should in the course of things have come to stand witness to this strange cure goes without saying.
curious.ja: すると蛮僧は、身動きをしてはいけないと云ふので、劉の体を細引で、ぐるぐる巻にした。それから、僮僕の一人に云ひつけて、酒を入れた素焼の瓶を一つ、劉の枕もとへ持つて来させた。当座の行きがかりで、糟邱の良友たる孫先生が、この不思議な療治に立合ふ事になつたのは云ふまでもない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: What sort of thing a wine worm is, what becomes of a man when it is no longer in his belly, what the jar of wine at his pillow is meant for, no one knows but the barbarian monk. Put so, Liu, going out naked into the blazing sun knowing nothing, may seem very heedless, but when ordinary men go through schooling and the like, in truth they are mostly doing much the same thing.
curious.ja: 酒虫と云ふ物が、どんな物だか、それが腹の中にゐなくなると、どうなるのだか、枕もとにある酒の瓶は、何にするつもりなのだか、それを知つてゐるのは、蛮僧の外に一人もない。かう云ふと、何も知らずに、炎天へ裸で出てゐる劉は、甚、迂濶なやうに思はれるが、普通の人間が、学校の教育などをうけるのも、実は大抵、これと同じやうな事をしてゐるのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: III
curious.ja: 三
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Hot. Sweat welled up prickling on his brow, and no sooner had it beaded than it ran lukewarm toward his eyes. As ill luck would have it, he was bound with thin cord, so of course he could not put out a hand to wipe it away. When he tried moving his neck to turn the sweat from its course, he felt at that instant a violent dizziness coming on, so to his regret he gave up that plan too. Meanwhile the sweat unceremoniously wet his eyelids and ran by the side of his nose and round his mouth to under his chin. Exceedingly nasty.
curious.ja: 暑い。額へ汗がぢりぢりと湧いて来て、それが玉になつたかと思ふと、つうつと生暖く、眼の方へ流れて来る。生憎、細引でしばられてゐるから、手を出して拭ふ訳には、勿論行かない。そこで、首を動かして、汗の進路を変へやうとすると、その途端に、はげしく眩暈がしさうな気がしたので、残念ながら、この計画も亦、見合せる事にした。その中に、汗は遠慮なく、眶をぬらして、鼻の側から口許をまはりながら、頤の下まで流れて行く。気味が悪い事夥しい。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Until then he had lain with his eyes open, staring hard at the sky scorched white and the hemp field with its drooping leaves, but once the sweat began to run unchecked he had to give even that up. It was then that Liu learned for the first time that sweat stings when it gets in the eyes. So with the face of a sheep in the slaughterhouse, he meekly shut his eyes and lay baking in the sun, and presently he began to feel a certain pain in the skin of every upturned part of him, face or body alike. Over the whole surface of the skin, forces seemed to be at work pulling in every direction, while the skin itself had not an ounce of elasticity to answer them. Everywhere prickled — that perhaps best describes the pain. This was not the misery of merely sweating. Liu began to find it a little hateful that he had taken the barbarian monk's cure.
curious.ja: それまでは、眼を開いて、白く焦された空や、葉をたらした麻畑を、まじ〳〵と眺めてゐたが、汗が無暗に流れるやうになつてからは、それさへ断念しなければならなくなつた。劉は、この時、始めて、汗が眼にはいると、しみるものだと云ふ事を、知つたのである。そこで、屠所の羊の様な顔をして、神妙に眼をつぶりながら、ぢつと日に照りつけられてゐると、今度は、顔と云はず体と云はず、上になつてゐる部分の皮膚が、次第に或痛みを感じるやうになつて来た。皮膚の全面に、あらゆる方向へ動かうとする力が働いてゐるが、皮膚自身は、それに対して、毫も弾力を持つてゐない。それでどこもかしこも、ぴり〳〵する――とでも説明したら、よからうと思ふ痛みである。これは、汗所の苦しさではない。劉は、少し蛮僧の治療をうけたのが、忌々しくなつて来た。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Yet, to think it over afterwards, this was still the part that was not so hard to bear. — Presently his throat grew thirsty. Liu too knew the story of how Cao Mengde or someone cured his soldiers of thirst by telling them there was a plum grove ahead. But now, however he called to mind the sweet-sour of plums, his thirst was none the less for it. He worked his chin and bit his tongue, but the inside of his mouth still held its heat. Even that would surely have been somewhat easier to bear if it had not been for the unglazed jar at his pillow. From the jar's mouth a rich scent of wine came without interruption, assailing Liu's nose. And, perhaps it was only fancy, but he felt the scent grow stronger with every minute. Thinking at least to look at the jar, Liu opened his eyes. Glancing upward with his eyes alone, all that came in sight were the mouth of the jar and perhaps half of its amply bulging body. That was all that came in sight, but at the same time there rose in Liu's imagining the sight of wine brimming undisturbed in the dim interior of the jar, the colour of gold. Before he knew it he licked his cracked lips all round with his dry tongue, but there was no sign at all of spittle welling up. Even his sweat by now had been dried out of him by the sun, and no longer ran as before.
curious.ja: しかし、これは、後になつて考へて見ると、まだ苦しくない方の部だつたのである。――そのうちに、喉が渇いて来た。劉も、曹孟徳か誰かが、前路に梅林ありと云つて、軍士の渇を医したと云ふ事は知つてゐる。が、今の場合、いくら、梅子の甘酸を念頭に浮べて見ても、喉の渇く事は、少しも前と変りがない。頤を動かして見たり、舌を噛んで見たりしたが、口の中は依然として熱を持つてゐる。それも、枕もとの素焼の瓶がなかつたら、まだ幾分でも、我慢がし易かつたのに違ひない。所が、瓶の口からは、芬々たる酒香が、間断なく、劉の鼻を襲つて来る。しかも、気のせいか、その酒香が、一分毎に、益々高くなつて来るやうな心もちさへする。劉は、せめて、瓶だけでも見ようと思つて、眼をあけた。上眼を使つて見ると、瓶の口と、応揚にふくれた胴の半分ばかりが、眼にはいる。眼にはいるのは、それだけであるが、同時に、劉の想像には、その瓶のうす暗い内部に、黄金のやうな色をした酒のなみ〳〵と湛へてゐる容子が、浮んで来た。思はず、ひびの出来た唇を、乾いた舌で舐めまはして見たが、唾の湧く気色は、更にない。汗さへ今では、日に干されて、前のやうには、流れなくなつてしまつた。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: A well-known Chinese anecdote: the general Cao Cao, on a thirsty march, told his men a plum grove lay ahead, and the thought of sour plums made their mouths water.
notes.span: there was a plum grove ahead

curious.en: Then a fierce dizziness came on, two or three times running. The headache had not let up since some time before. In his heart Liu resented the barbarian monk more and more. And he thought, too, why a man such as himself should have let himself be talked round by such a fellow into bearing such witless suffering. Meanwhile his throat grew thirstier still. His chest turned strangely queasy. He could no longer bear to lie still. At last, resolved, he opened his panting mouth, meaning to ask the barbarian monk at his pillow to call the cure off. —
curious.ja: すると、はげしい眩暈が、つづいて、二三度起つた。頭痛はさつきから、しつきりなしにしてゐる。劉は、心の中で愈、蛮僧を怨めしく思つた。それから又何故、自分ともあるものが、あんな人間の口車に乗つて、こんな莫迦げた苦しみをするのだらうとも思つた。そのうちに、喉は、益々、渇いて来る。胸は妙にむかついて来る。もう我慢にも、ぢつとしてはゐられない。そこで劉はとう〳〵思切つて、枕もとの蛮僧に、療治の中止を申込むつもりで、喘ぎながら、口を開いた。――
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: At that very instant. Liu began to feel some unnameable lump creeping little by little from his chest up toward his throat. At one moment it seemed to writhe like an earthworm, at another to edge itself along little by little like a gecko. In any case, a soft thing, soft as it was, came squirming and pressing its way up the gullet. And at last, when it had forced its way past below the Adam's apple, it suddenly slipped out of the dark, slimy like a loach or something, and flew outwards with force.
curious.ja: すると、その途端である。劉は、何とも知れない塊が、少しづゝ胸から喉へ這ひ上つて来るのを感じ出した。それが或は蚯蚓のやうに、蠕動してゐるかと思ふと、或は守宮のやうに、少しづゝ居ざつてゐるやうでもある。兎に角或柔い物が、柔いなりに、むづりむづりと、食道を上へせり上つて来るのである。さうしてとうとうしまひに、それが、喉仏の下を、無理にすりぬけたと思ふと、今度はいきなり、鰌か何かのやうにぬるりと暗い所をぬけ出して、勢よく外へとんで出た。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: With that, from the familiar unglazed jar, there came a faint plip, as of something dropping into the wine.
curious.ja: と、その拍子に、例の素焼の瓶の方で、ぽちやりと、何か酒の中へ落ちるやうな音がした。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: At that the barbarian monk suddenly lifted the haunches he had settled and began to undo the thin cord wound about Liu's body. The wine worm was out, he said, so Liu might set his mind at rest.
curious.ja: すると、蛮僧が、急に落ちつけてゐた尻を持ち上げて、劉の体にかゝつてゐる、細引を解きはじめた。もう、酒虫が出たから、安心しろと云ふのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: "Is it out?" Liu said as if groaning, lifting his swimming head, and from mere curiosity, forgetting even his thirst, crawled naked as he was to the side of the jar. At the sight, Sun Sensei too came hurrying toward the two, warding off the sun with his white-feather fan. When all three peered together into the jar, a thing like a small salamander, the colour of its flesh like red mud, was swimming in the wine. It may have been about three sun long. It had a mouth, it had eyes. Somehow, as it swam, it seemed to be drinking the wine. When Liu saw this, his stomach turned suddenly....
curious.ja: 「出ましたかな。」劉は、呻くやうにかう云つて、ふらふらする頭を起しながら、物珍しさの余り、喉の渇いたのも忘れて、裸のまま、瓶の側へ這ひよつた。それと見ると、孫先生も、白羽扇で日をよけながら、急いで、二人の方へやつて来る。さて、三人揃つて瓶の中を覗きこむと、肉の色が朱泥に似た、小さな山椒魚のやうなものが、酒の中を泳いでゐる。長さは、三寸ばかりであらう。口もあれば、眼もある。どうやら、泳ぎながら、酒を飲んでゐるらしい。劉はこれを見ると、急に胸が悪くなつた。……
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: A sun is a traditional unit of length, about three centimetres. Three sun is roughly nine centimetres long.

curious.en: IV
curious.ja: 四
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The barbarian monk's cure showed itself at once. From that day Liu Dacheng abruptly became unable to drink wine. Now, he says, he dislikes even the smell of it. Yet strangely, from that time Liu's health began little by little to fail. This year makes three years since he spat out the wine worm, and nowhere remains a trace of the round, fat figure of former years. Skin of poor lustre, still oily, wraps the harsh bones of his face, and frost-touched locks linger only faintly above his temples, and there is said to be no counting how many times in the year he now takes to his bed.
curious.ja: 蛮僧の治療の効は、覿面に現れた。劉大成は、その日から、ぱつたり酒が飲めなくなつたのである。今は、匂を嗅ぐのも、嫌だと云ふ。所が、不思議な事に、劉の健康が、それから、少しづつ、衰へて来た。今年で、酒虫を吐いてから、三年になるが、往年の丸丸と肥つてゐた俤は、何処にもない。色光沢の悪い皮膚が、脂じみたまま、険しい顔の骨を包んで、霜に侵された双髩が、纔に、顳顬の上に、残つてゐるばかり、一年の中に、何度、床につくか、わからない位ださうである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: But Liu's health was not the only thing that failed after that. Liu's fortune too has declined with gathering speed, and now the fields by the city wall, counted at three hundred mu, have for the most part passed into other hands. Liu himself, of necessity, has taken a plough in unpractised hands and lives out his wretched days, day by day.
curious.ja: しかし、それ以来、衰へたのは、劉の健康ばかりではない。劉の家産も亦とんとん拍子に傾いて、今では、三百畝を以て数へた負郭の田も、多くは人の手に渡つた。劉自身も、余儀なく、馴れない手に鋤を執つて、佗しいその日その日を送つてゐるのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Since he spat out the wine worm, why did Liu's health fail? Why did his fortune decline — once the spitting of the wine worm and Liu's later ruin are set side by side as cause and effect, this is a question that readily occurs to anyone. Indeed this question has been repeated by people of every occupation living in Changshan, and from their mouths answers of every kind have been given. The three answers given here are in truth no more than the most representative chosen from among them.
curious.ja: 酒虫を吐いて以来、何故、劉の健康が衰へたか。何故、家産が傾いたか――酒虫を吐いたと云ふ事と、劉のその後の零落とを、因果の関係に並べて見る以上、これは、誰にでも起りやすい疑問である。現にこの疑問は、長山に住んでゐる、あらゆる職業の人人によつて繰返され、且、それらの人人の口から、あらゆる種類の答を与へられた。今、ここに挙げる三つの答も、実はその中から、最、代表的なものを選んだのに過ぎない。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The first answer. The wine worm was Liu's fortune, and not Liu's disease. By chancing to meet an ignorant barbarian monk, he willingly brought about the loss of this heaven-given fortune.
curious.ja: 第一の答。酒虫は、劉の福であつて、劉の病ではない。偶、暗愚の蛮僧に遇つた為に、好んで、この天与の福を失ふやうな事になつたのである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The second answer. The wine worm was Liu's disease, and not Liu's fortune. For to empty a whole jar at a single drinking is quite beyond what an ordinary man can conceive. Had the wine worm not been removed, Liu must undoubtedly have died before long. Seen in this light, poverty and sickness arriving each in turn should rather be called happiness for Liu.
curious.ja: 第二の答。酒虫は、劉の病であつて、劉の福ではない。何故と云へば、一飲一甕を尽すなどと云ふ事は、到底、常人の考へられない所だからである。そこで、もし酒虫を除かなかつたなら、劉は必久しからずして、死んだのに相違ない。して見ると、貧病、迭に至るのも、寧劉にとつては、幸福と云ふべきである。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: The third answer. The wine worm was neither Liu's disease nor Liu's fortune. Liu from of old did nothing but drink. If wine were taken away from Liu's life, nothing would remain behind. Seen in this light, Liu is the wine worm, and the wine worm is Liu. Hence Liu's casting off the wine worm was the same as killing himself. That is to say, from the day he became unable to drink, Liu is Liu and yet is not Liu. If Liu himself were already gone, then it is entirely natural, and only to be expected, that the health and fortune of the Liu of former days should have been lost.
curious.ja: 第三の答。酒虫は、劉の病でもなければ、劉の福でもない。劉は、昔から酒ばかり飲んでゐた。劉の一生から酒を除けば、後には、何も残らない。して見ると、劉は即酒虫、酒虫は即劉である。だから、劉が酒虫を去つたのは自ら己を殺したのも同前である。つまり、酒が飲めなくなつた日から、劉は劉にして、劉ではない。劉自身が既になくなつてゐたとしたら、昔日の劉の健康なり家産なりが、失はれたのも、至極、当然な話であらう。
curious.label: house-checked

curious.en: Which of these answers best hits the mark, I myself do not know. I have done no more than list such moral judgements at the end of this tale, in imitation of the *Didacticism* of the Chinese novelists.
curious.ja: これらの答の中で、どれが、最よく、当を得てゐるか、それは自分にもわからない。自分は、唯、支那の小説家の Didacticism に倣つて、かう云ふ道徳的な判断を、この話の最後に、列挙して見たまでゝある。
curious.label: house-checked

notes.body: The word appears in English in the original. It points to the habit of Chinese popular novels of closing with an explicit moral.

curious.en: — Fourth month of the fifth year —
curious.ja: ――五年四月――
curious.label: house-checked

student.en: I
student.ja: 一
student.label: house-checked

student.en: It was a heat such as had not been known for years. Wherever one looked, the roof-tiles of the houses, set hard with mud, threw back the sunlight dully, like lead, and even the swallows' nests hung beneath them seemed, at this rate, likely to steam the chicks and eggs inside them alive where they lay. Still more, every field that was a field, whether hemp or millet, hung its head limply in the reek of the earth, and there was not one thing that, green as it was, was not wilted. The sky seen above those fields, perhaps stricken with the closeness of these past days, though fair, hung thick and turbid in the air near the ground, and here and there mere shapes of towering cloud, like hail parched in a roasting pan, floated in lumps. — The tale of the "wine worm" begins with three men who have gone out of their way into the threshing-yard in the blazing sun in such weather.
student.ja: 近年にない暑さである。どこを見ても、泥で固めた家々の屋根瓦が、鉛のやうに鈍く日の光を反射して、その下に懸けてある燕の巣さへ、この塩梅では中にゐる雛や卵を、そのまゝ蒸殺してしまふかと思はれる。まして、畑と云ふ畑は、麻でも黍でも、皆、土いきれにぐつたりと頭をさげて、何一つ、青いなりに、萎れてゐないものはない。その畑の上に見える空も、この頃の温気に中てられたせいか、地上に近い大気は、晴れながら、どんよりと濁つて、その所々に、霰を炮烙で煎つたやうな、形ばかりの雲の峰が、つぶつぶと浮かんでゐる。――「酒虫」の話は、この陽気に、わざ〳〵炎天の打麦場へ出てゐる、三人の男で始まるのである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Strangely, one of them lay naked, on his back upon the bare ground. What was more, for some reason, his hands and his feet were wound round and round with thin cord. Yet the man himself showed no particular sign of minding it. He was a short man, of good colour, somehow giving a sense of dull heaviness, fat as a pig. Then a handy unglazed jar stood at this man's pillow, but what was inside that, too, was not to be known.
student.ja: 不思議な事に、その中の一人は、素裸で、仰向けに地面へ寝ころんでゐる。おまけに、どう云ふ訳だか、細引で、手も足もぐる〳〵巻にされてゐる。が格別当人は、それを苦に病んでゐる容子もない。背の低い、血色の好い、どことなく鈍重と云ふ感じを起させる、豚のやうに肥つた男である。それから手ごろな素焼の瓶が一つ、この男の枕もとに置いてあるが、これも中に何がはいつてゐるのだか、わからない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Another was a monk in a yellow robe, with a small bronze ring hung from his ear, of a strangely antique visage at first sight. His skin was dark beyond the common, and, to see the curl of his hair and beard, he seemed a man come from somewhere west of the Congling. For some time he had been patiently waving a red-handled fly-whisk to drive off the horseflies and flies that would fasten upon the naked man, but, grown a little tired at last, as it seemed, he had now come beside that same unglazed jar and squatted there with pompous self-importance, like a turkey.
student.ja: もう一人は、黄色い法衣を着て、耳に小さな青銅の環をさげた、一見、象貌の奇古な沙門である。皮膚の色が並はづれて黒い上に、髪や鬚の縮れてゐる所を見ると、どうも葱嶺の西からでも来た人間らしい。これはさつきから根気よく、朱柄の麈尾をふりふり、裸の男にたからうとする虻や蠅を追つてゐたが、流石に少しくたびれたと見えて、今では、例の素焼の瓶の側へ来て、七面鳥のやうな恰好をしながら、勿体らしくしやがんでゐる。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: The last stood far apart from the other two, under the eaves of a thatched hut in the corner of the threshing-yard. This man grew on the tip of his chin, as a mere token, a beard like a rat's tail, and his get-up was a black-cloth gown long enough to hide his heels, with a tea-brown sash whose knot hung slack. From the careful way he plied from time to time a fan made of white birds' feathers, he was probably a Confucian scholar or something of the sort.
student.ja: あとの一人は、この二人からずつと離れて、打麦場の隅にある草房の軒下に立つてゐる。この男は、頤の先に、鼠の尻尾のやうな髯を、申訳だけに生やして、踵が隠れる程長い皁布衫に、結目をだらしなく垂らした茶褐帯と云ふ拵へである。白い鳥の羽で製つた団扇を、時々大事さうに使つてゐる容子では、多分、儒者か何かにちがひない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: All three alike kept their mouths shut as if by agreement. Nor did they so much as stir, as though they took some uncommon interest in whatever was about to happen, and for that held their breath.
student.ja: この三人が三人とも、云ひ合せたやうに、口を噤んでゐる。その上、碌に身動きさへもしない、何か、これから起らうとする事に、非常な興味でも持つてゐて、その為に、皆、息をひそめてゐるのではないかと思はれる。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: It must have been exactly noon. The dogs too, perhaps sunk in their midday doze, were not heard to bark once. The hemp and millet ringing the threshing-yard shone their green leaves in the sun and stood hushed and perfectly still. And the sky seen beyond them, all stifling heat, trailed a shimmering haze, so that one might have doubted whether even the towering clouds were panting in this drought. Look where one would, nothing seemed to breathe but these three men. And those three kept their silence like the clay images enshrined in the Guandi Temple. . . .
student.ja: 日は正に、亭午であらう。犬も午睡をしてゐるせいか、吠える声一つ聞えない。打麦場を囲んでゐる麻や黍も、青い葉を日に光らせて、ひつそりかんと静まつてゐる。それから、その末に見える空も、一面に、熱くるしく、炎靄をたゞよはせて、雲の峰さへもこの旱に、肩息をついてゐるのかと、疑はれる。見渡した所、息が通つてゐるらしいのは、この三人の男の外にない。さうして、その三人が又、関帝廟に安置してある、泥塑の像のやうに沈黙を守つてゐる。……
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Of course, this is no tale of Japan. — It is what happened one summer on the threshing-yard of the Liu family at a place called Changshan in China.
student.ja: 勿論、日本の話ではない。――支那の長山と云ふ所にある劉氏の打麦場で、或年の夏、起つた出来事である。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: II
student.ja: 二
student.label: house-checked

student.en: The man lying naked in the blazing sun was the master of this threshing-yard, surnamed Liu and named Dacheng, one of the leading men of fortune in Changshan. This man's one indulgence was drink, and from morning on he was scarcely ever parted from the cup. And that, "whenever he drank alone, he finished a whole jar," was a capacity beyond ordinary men. Though, as already said, "three hundred mu of fields by the city wall, half planted with millet," so there was not the least fear that drink would burden his estate.
student.ja: 裸で、炎天に寝ころんでゐるのは、この打麦場の主人で、姓は劉、名は大成と云ふ、長山では、屈指の素封家の一人である。この男の道楽は、酒を飲む一方で、朝から、殆、盃を離したと云ふ事がない。それも、「独酌する毎に輒、一甕を尽す」と云ふのだから、人並をはづれた酒量である。尤も前にも云つたやうに、「負郭の田三百畝、半は黍を種う」と云ふので、飲の為に家産が累はされるやうな惧は、万々ない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Why he should be lying naked in the blazing sun has a history behind it, as follows. — That day, as Liu, together with Sun Sensei, his fellow drinker (this is the scholar who had held the white-feather fan), was fighting out a game on the board, leaning against the bamboo wife in a well-aired room, the maidservant came and said, "A monk, lodging they say at Hodoji or somewhere, has just come and insists upon seeing the master. What shall I do?"
student.ja: それが、何故、裸で、炎天に寝ころんでゐるかと云ふと、それには、かう云ふ因縁がある。――その日、劉が、同じ飲仲間の孫先生と一しよに（これが、白羽扇を持つてゐた儒者である。）風通しのいゝ室で、竹婦人に靠れながら、棋局を闘はせてゐると、召使ひの丫鬟が来て、「唯今、宝幢寺とかにゐると云ふ、坊さんが御見えになりまして、是非、御主人に御目にかゝりたいと申しますが、いかゞ致しませう。」と云ふ。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "What, Hodoji?" So saying, Liu blinked his small eyes as if dazzled, and then, heaving up his fat body, hot-looking in itself, ordered, "Then show him in here." Then, with a glance at Sun Sensei's face, he added, "It must be that monk, I suppose."
student.ja: 「なに、宝幢寺？」かう云つて、劉は小さな眼を、まぶしさうに、しばたたいたが、やがて、暑さうに肥つた体を起しながら、「では、こゝへ御通し申せ。」と云ひつけた。それから、孫先生の顔をちよいと見て「大方あの坊主でせう。」とつけ加へた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: The monk lodging at Hodoji was a barbarian monk come from the Western Regions. As he both practised medicine and administered the arts of the bedchamber, his repute stood high in these parts. For instance, rumours all but miraculous were going round in full force, that Zhang San's black cataract had suddenly taken a turn for the better, that Li Si's byouen had been healed on the spot. — Both men had heard these rumours. With what business could that barbarian monk now have gone out of his way to come to Liu's house? Of course Liu had no recollection at all of having sent to fetch him.
student.ja: 宝幢寺にゐる坊主と云ふのは、西域から来た蛮僧である。これが、医療も加へれば、房術も施すと云ふので、この界隈では、評判が高い。たとへば、張三の黒内障が、忽、快方に向つたとか、李四の病閹が、即座に平癒したとか、殆、奇蹟に近い噂が盛に行はれてゐるのである。――この噂は、二人とも聞いてゐた。その蛮僧が、今、何の用で、わざわざ、劉の所へ出むいて来たのであらう。勿論、劉の方から、迎へにやつた覚えなどは、全然ない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Let it be said in passing that Liu was not, by nature, a man who delighted in visitors. But when he already had one guest with him, and a new visitor came, he would generally receive him readily enough. He had what might be called a childish vanity, as if to boast before his guest of having guests. Besides, today's barbarian monk was just now talked of wherever one went. By no means a visitor to be ashamed of meeting. — Liu's motive in proposing to meet him lay much in this direction.
student.ja: 序に云つて置くが、劉は、一体、来客を悦ぶやうな男ではない。が、他に一人、来客がある場合に、新来の客が来たとなると、大抵ならば、快く会つてやる。客の手前、客のあるのを自慢するとでも云つたらよささうな、小供らしい虚栄心を持つてゐるからである。それに、今日の蛮僧は、この頃、どこででも評判になつてゐる。決して、会つて恥しいやうな客ではない。――劉が会はうと云ひ出した動機は、大体こんな所にあつたのである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "What can his business be?"
student.ja: 「何の用でせう。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Begging, most likely. He will be asking us to bestow some alms, I suppose."
student.ja: 「まづ、物貰ひですな。信施でもしてくれと云ふのでせう。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: While the two were talking such matters over, presently there entered, led by the maidservant, as they looked, a strange-formed monk, tall and with eyes like faceted amethyst. He wore a yellow robe, his grown-out curling hair hanging heavily, as if a nuisance, over his shoulders. Fly-whisk with its red handle in hand, he planted himself heavily in the middle of the room. He offered no greeting and said not a word.
student.ja: こんな事を、二人で話してゐる内に、やがて、丫鬟の案内で、はいつて来たのを見ると、背の高い、紫石稜のやうな眼をした、異形な沙門である。黄色い法衣を着て、その肩に、縮れた髪の伸びたのを、うるささうに垂らしてゐる。それが、朱柄の麈尾を持つたまゝ、のつそり室のまん中に立つた。挨拶もしなければ、口もきかない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Liu hung back for a while, but as the silence grew somehow uneasy, he ventured, "Have you some business with me?"
student.ja: 劉は、しばらく、ためらつてゐたが、その内に、それが何となく、不安になつて来たので「何か御用かな。」と訊いて見た。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: At which the barbarian monk said, "You are the one, are you not, who is fond of drink."
student.ja: すると、蛮僧が云つた。「あなたでせうな、酒が好きなのは。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Indeed." The question came so abruptly that Liu gave a vague answer, looking toward Sun Sensei as if seeking rescue. Sun Sensei, with a composed face, went on placing stones on the board by himself. He showed no disposition whatever to take part.
student.ja: 「さやう。」劉は、あまり問が唐突なので、曖昧な返事をしながら、救を求めるやうに、孫先生の方を見た。孫先生は、すまして、独りで、盤面に石を下してゐる。まるで、取り合ふ容子はない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "You are afflicted with a rare disease. Are you aware of it?" The barbarian monk said this as if to press the point. Hearing of a disease, Liu wore a dubious look, stroking the bamboo wife as he did so—
student.ja: 「あなたは、珍しい病に罹つて御出になる。それを御存知ですかな。」蛮僧は念を押すやうに、かう云つた。劉は、病と聞いたので、けげんな顔をして、竹婦人を撫でながら、
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "A disease— is it?"
student.ja: 「病――ですかな。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "It is."
student.ja: 「さうです。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "No, ever since I was a child . . ." As Liu was about to say something, the barbarian monk cut him off.
student.ja: 「いや、幼少の時から……」劉が何か云はうとすると、蛮僧はそれを遮つて、
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Drink as you may, you never get drunk, do you?"
student.ja: 「酒を飲まれても、酔ひますまいな。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: " . . ." Liu stared hard at the other's face and shut his mouth. In fact, drink as he might, this man had never been drunk.
student.ja: 「……」劉は、ぢろぢろ、相手の顔を見ながら、口を噤んでしまつた。実際この男は、いくら酒を飲んでも、酔つた事がないのである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "That is the proof of the disease," the barbarian monk went on with a faint smile. "There is a wine worm in your belly. Unless it is removed, this disease will not be cured. This poor monk has come to cure your disease."
student.ja: 「それが、病の証拠ですよ。」蛮僧は、うす笑をしながら、語をついで、「腹中に酒虫がゐる。それを除かないと、この病は癒りません。貧道は、あなたの病を癒しに来たのです。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Can it be cured?" Liu let out the words in an uncertain voice before he knew it. And he was ashamed of himself for it.
student.ja: 「癒りますかな。」劉は思はず覚束なさうな声を出した。さうして、自分でそれを恥ぢた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "It is because it can be cured that I have come."
student.ja: 「癒ればこそ、来ましたが。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Then Sun Sensei, who until now had listened in silence to the exchange, suddenly put in a word.
student.ja: すると、今まで、黙つて、問答を聞いてゐた孫先生が、急に語を挟んだ。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Will you be using some medicine?"
student.ja: 「何か、薬でも御用ひか。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "No, there will be no need to use anything like medicine," the barbarian monk answered curtly.
student.ja: 「いや、薬なぞは用ひるまでもありません。」蛮僧は不愛想に、かう答へた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Sun Sensei, to begin with, despised the two teachings of Dao and Buddha with scarcely any reason. So even when thrown together with a Daoist priest or a monk, he had very rarely exchanged a word. That he should now suddenly feel moved to speak was wholly because the words "wine worm" had caught his interest; fond of wine himself, on hearing this he had grown a little uneasy lest there be a wine worm in his own belly too. When he heard the barbarian monk's grudging answer, however, he suddenly felt as if he had been made a fool of, so with a slight frown he began once more, in silence as before, to place his stones. And at the same time, inwardly, he thought his host Liu a fool for meeting with so insolent a monk.
student.ja: 孫先生は、元来、道仏の二教を殆、無理由に軽蔑してゐる。だから、道士とか僧侶とかと一しよになつても、口をきいた事は滅多にない。それが、今ふと口を出す気になつたのは、全く酒虫と云ふ語の興味に動かされたからで、酒の好きな先生は、これを聞くと、自分の腹の中にも、酒虫がゐはしないかと、聊、不安になつて来たのである。所が、蛮僧の不承不承な答を聞くと、急に、自分が莫迦にされたやうな気がしたので、先生はちよいと顔をしかめながら、又元の通り、黙々として棋子を下しはじめた。さうして、それと同時に、内心、こんな横柄な坊主に会つたり何ぞする主人の劉を、莫迦げてゐると思ひ出した。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: For his part, Liu of course paid no mind to any such thing.
student.ja: 劉の方では、勿論そんな事には頓着しない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Then will you use needles?"
student.ja: 「では、針でも使ひますかな。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "What, it is a far simpler matter than that."
student.ja: 「なに、もつと造作のない事です。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Then is it an incantation?"
student.ja: 「では呪ですかな。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "No, nor is it any incantation."
student.ja: 「いや、呪でもありません。」
student.label: house-checked

student.en: After repeating such exchanges, the barbarian monk briefly explained his cure to them. — According to it, he had only to strip naked and lie still in the sun. To Liu this seemed a very easy thing. If he could be cured by that much, there was nothing better than to be cured. Moreover, without himself knowing it, he was a little moved by curiosity at the point of submitting to the barbarian monk's treatment.
student.ja: かう云ふ会話を繰返した末に、蛮僧は、簡単に、その療法を説明して聞かせた。――それによるに、唯、裸になつて、日向にぢつとしてゐさへすればよいと云ふのである。劉には、それが、甚、容易な事のやうに思はれた。その位の事で癒るなら、癒して貰ふのに越した事はない。その上、意識してはゐなかつたが、蛮僧の治療を受けると云ふ点で、好奇心も少しは動いてゐた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: So at last Liu was the first to bow his head, and it came to his saying, "Then let me ask you to cure me." — There is such a history behind Liu's lying naked in the threshing-yard in the blazing sun.
student.ja: そこでとうとう、劉も、こつちから頭を下げて、「では、どうか一つ、癒して頂きませう。」と云ふ事になつた。――劉が、裸で、炎天の打麦場にねころんでゐるのには、かう云ふ謂れが、あるのである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Then, telling him not to move, the barbarian monk wound Liu's body round and round with thin cord. Then he bade one of the servants bring an unglazed jar filled with wine to Liu's pillow. That Sun Sensei, good friend of the wine mound, should in the course of things have come to stand witness to this strange cure goes without saying.
student.ja: すると蛮僧は、身動きをしてはいけないと云ふので、劉の体を細引で、ぐるぐる巻にした。それから、僮僕の一人に云ひつけて、酒を入れた素焼の瓶を一つ、劉の枕もとへ持つて来させた。当座の行きがかりで、糟邱の良友たる孫先生が、この不思議な療治に立合ふ事になつたのは云ふまでもない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: What sort of thing a wine worm is, what becomes of a man when it is no longer in his belly, what the jar of wine at his pillow is meant for, no one knows but the barbarian monk. Put so, Liu, going out naked into the blazing sun knowing nothing, may seem very heedless, but when ordinary men go through schooling and the like, in truth they are mostly doing much the same thing.
student.ja: 酒虫と云ふ物が、どんな物だか、それが腹の中にゐなくなると、どうなるのだか、枕もとにある酒の瓶は、何にするつもりなのだか、それを知つてゐるのは、蛮僧の外に一人もない。かう云ふと、何も知らずに、炎天へ裸で出てゐる劉は、甚、迂濶なやうに思はれるが、普通の人間が、学校の教育などをうけるのも、実は大抵、これと同じやうな事をしてゐるのである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: III
student.ja: 三
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Hot. Sweat welled up prickling on his brow, and no sooner had it beaded than it ran lukewarm toward his eyes. As ill luck would have it, he was bound with thin cord, so of course he could not put out a hand to wipe it away. When he tried moving his neck to turn the sweat from its course, he felt at that instant a violent dizziness coming on, so to his regret he gave up that plan too. Meanwhile the sweat unceremoniously wet his eyelids and ran by the side of his nose and round his mouth to under his chin. Exceedingly nasty.
student.ja: 暑い。額へ汗がぢりぢりと湧いて来て、それが玉になつたかと思ふと、つうつと生暖く、眼の方へ流れて来る。生憎、細引でしばられてゐるから、手を出して拭ふ訳には、勿論行かない。そこで、首を動かして、汗の進路を変へやうとすると、その途端に、はげしく眩暈がしさうな気がしたので、残念ながら、この計画も亦、見合せる事にした。その中に、汗は遠慮なく、眶をぬらして、鼻の側から口許をまはりながら、頤の下まで流れて行く。気味が悪い事夥しい。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Until then he had lain with his eyes open, staring hard at the sky scorched white and the hemp field with its drooping leaves, but once the sweat began to run unchecked he had to give even that up. It was then that Liu learned for the first time that sweat stings when it gets in the eyes. So with the face of a sheep in the slaughterhouse, he meekly shut his eyes and lay baking in the sun, and presently he began to feel a certain pain in the skin of every upturned part of him, face or body alike. Over the whole surface of the skin, forces seemed to be at work pulling in every direction, while the skin itself had not an ounce of elasticity to answer them. Everywhere prickled — that perhaps best describes the pain. This was not the misery of merely sweating. Liu began to find it a little hateful that he had taken the barbarian monk's cure.
student.ja: それまでは、眼を開いて、白く焦された空や、葉をたらした麻畑を、まじ〳〵と眺めてゐたが、汗が無暗に流れるやうになつてからは、それさへ断念しなければならなくなつた。劉は、この時、始めて、汗が眼にはいると、しみるものだと云ふ事を、知つたのである。そこで、屠所の羊の様な顔をして、神妙に眼をつぶりながら、ぢつと日に照りつけられてゐると、今度は、顔と云はず体と云はず、上になつてゐる部分の皮膚が、次第に或痛みを感じるやうになつて来た。皮膚の全面に、あらゆる方向へ動かうとする力が働いてゐるが、皮膚自身は、それに対して、毫も弾力を持つてゐない。それでどこもかしこも、ぴり〳〵する――とでも説明したら、よからうと思ふ痛みである。これは、汗所の苦しさではない。劉は、少し蛮僧の治療をうけたのが、忌々しくなつて来た。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Yet, to think it over afterwards, this was still the part that was not so hard to bear. — Presently his throat grew thirsty. Liu too knew the story of how Cao Mengde or someone cured his soldiers of thirst by telling them there was a plum grove ahead. But now, however he called to mind the sweet-sour of plums, his thirst was none the less for it. He worked his chin and bit his tongue, but the inside of his mouth still held its heat. Even that would surely have been somewhat easier to bear if it had not been for the unglazed jar at his pillow. From the jar's mouth a rich scent of wine came without interruption, assailing Liu's nose. And, perhaps it was only fancy, but he felt the scent grow stronger with every minute. Thinking at least to look at the jar, Liu opened his eyes. Glancing upward with his eyes alone, all that came in sight were the mouth of the jar and perhaps half of its amply bulging body. That was all that came in sight, but at the same time there rose in Liu's imagining the sight of wine brimming undisturbed in the dim interior of the jar, the colour of gold. Before he knew it he licked his cracked lips all round with his dry tongue, but there was no sign at all of spittle welling up. Even his sweat by now had been dried out of him by the sun, and no longer ran as before.
student.ja: しかし、これは、後になつて考へて見ると、まだ苦しくない方の部だつたのである。――そのうちに、喉が渇いて来た。劉も、曹孟徳か誰かが、前路に梅林ありと云つて、軍士の渇を医したと云ふ事は知つてゐる。が、今の場合、いくら、梅子の甘酸を念頭に浮べて見ても、喉の渇く事は、少しも前と変りがない。頤を動かして見たり、舌を噛んで見たりしたが、口の中は依然として熱を持つてゐる。それも、枕もとの素焼の瓶がなかつたら、まだ幾分でも、我慢がし易かつたのに違ひない。所が、瓶の口からは、芬々たる酒香が、間断なく、劉の鼻を襲つて来る。しかも、気のせいか、その酒香が、一分毎に、益々高くなつて来るやうな心もちさへする。劉は、せめて、瓶だけでも見ようと思つて、眼をあけた。上眼を使つて見ると、瓶の口と、応揚にふくれた胴の半分ばかりが、眼にはいる。眼にはいるのは、それだけであるが、同時に、劉の想像には、その瓶のうす暗い内部に、黄金のやうな色をした酒のなみ〳〵と湛へてゐる容子が、浮んで来た。思はず、ひびの出来た唇を、乾いた舌で舐めまはして見たが、唾の湧く気色は、更にない。汗さへ今では、日に干されて、前のやうには、流れなくなつてしまつた。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Then a fierce dizziness came on, two or three times running. The headache had not let up since some time before. In his heart Liu resented the barbarian monk more and more. And he thought, too, why a man such as himself should have let himself be talked round by such a fellow into bearing such witless suffering. Meanwhile his throat grew thirstier still. His chest turned strangely queasy. He could no longer bear to lie still. At last, resolved, he opened his panting mouth, meaning to ask the barbarian monk at his pillow to call the cure off. —
student.ja: すると、はげしい眩暈が、つづいて、二三度起つた。頭痛はさつきから、しつきりなしにしてゐる。劉は、心の中で愈、蛮僧を怨めしく思つた。それから又何故、自分ともあるものが、あんな人間の口車に乗つて、こんな莫迦げた苦しみをするのだらうとも思つた。そのうちに、喉は、益々、渇いて来る。胸は妙にむかついて来る。もう我慢にも、ぢつとしてはゐられない。そこで劉はとう〳〵思切つて、枕もとの蛮僧に、療治の中止を申込むつもりで、喘ぎながら、口を開いた。――
student.label: house-checked

student.en: At that very instant. Liu began to feel some unnameable lump creeping little by little from his chest up toward his throat. At one moment it seemed to writhe like an earthworm, at another to edge itself along little by little like a gecko. In any case, a soft thing, soft as it was, came squirming and pressing its way up the gullet. And at last, when it had forced its way past below the Adam's apple, it suddenly slipped out of the dark, slimy like a loach or something, and flew outwards with force.
student.ja: すると、その途端である。劉は、何とも知れない塊が、少しづゝ胸から喉へ這ひ上つて来るのを感じ出した。それが或は蚯蚓のやうに、蠕動してゐるかと思ふと、或は守宮のやうに、少しづゝ居ざつてゐるやうでもある。兎に角或柔い物が、柔いなりに、むづりむづりと、食道を上へせり上つて来るのである。さうしてとうとうしまひに、それが、喉仏の下を、無理にすりぬけたと思ふと、今度はいきなり、鰌か何かのやうにぬるりと暗い所をぬけ出して、勢よく外へとんで出た。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: With that, from the familiar unglazed jar, there came a faint plip, as of something dropping into the wine.
student.ja: と、その拍子に、例の素焼の瓶の方で、ぽちやりと、何か酒の中へ落ちるやうな音がした。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: At that the barbarian monk suddenly lifted the haunches he had settled and began to undo the thin cord wound about Liu's body. The wine worm was out, he said, so Liu might set his mind at rest.
student.ja: すると、蛮僧が、急に落ちつけてゐた尻を持ち上げて、劉の体にかゝつてゐる、細引を解きはじめた。もう、酒虫が出たから、安心しろと云ふのである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: "Is it out?" Liu said as if groaning, lifting his swimming head, and from mere curiosity, forgetting even his thirst, crawled naked as he was to the side of the jar. At the sight, Sun Sensei too came hurrying toward the two, warding off the sun with his white-feather fan. When all three peered together into the jar, a thing like a small salamander, the colour of its flesh like red mud, was swimming in the wine. It may have been about three sun long. It had a mouth, it had eyes. Somehow, as it swam, it seemed to be drinking the wine. When Liu saw this, his stomach turned suddenly....
student.ja: 「出ましたかな。」劉は、呻くやうにかう云つて、ふらふらする頭を起しながら、物珍しさの余り、喉の渇いたのも忘れて、裸のまま、瓶の側へ這ひよつた。それと見ると、孫先生も、白羽扇で日をよけながら、急いで、二人の方へやつて来る。さて、三人揃つて瓶の中を覗きこむと、肉の色が朱泥に似た、小さな山椒魚のやうなものが、酒の中を泳いでゐる。長さは、三寸ばかりであらう。口もあれば、眼もある。どうやら、泳ぎながら、酒を飲んでゐるらしい。劉はこれを見ると、急に胸が悪くなつた。……
student.label: house-checked

student.en: IV
student.ja: 四
student.label: house-checked

student.en: The barbarian monk's cure showed itself at once. From that day Liu Dacheng abruptly became unable to drink wine. Now, he says, he dislikes even the smell of it. Yet strangely, from that time Liu's health began little by little to fail. This year makes three years since he spat out the wine worm, and nowhere remains a trace of the round, fat figure of former years. Skin of poor lustre, still oily, wraps the harsh bones of his face, and frost-touched locks linger only faintly above his temples, and there is said to be no counting how many times in the year he now takes to his bed.
student.ja: 蛮僧の治療の効は、覿面に現れた。劉大成は、その日から、ぱつたり酒が飲めなくなつたのである。今は、匂を嗅ぐのも、嫌だと云ふ。所が、不思議な事に、劉の健康が、それから、少しづつ、衰へて来た。今年で、酒虫を吐いてから、三年になるが、往年の丸丸と肥つてゐた俤は、何処にもない。色光沢の悪い皮膚が、脂じみたまま、険しい顔の骨を包んで、霜に侵された双髩が、纔に、顳顬の上に、残つてゐるばかり、一年の中に、何度、床につくか、わからない位ださうである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: But Liu's health was not the only thing that failed after that. Liu's fortune too has declined with gathering speed, and now the fields by the city wall, counted at three hundred mu, have for the most part passed into other hands. Liu himself, of necessity, has taken a plough in unpractised hands and lives out his wretched days, day by day.
student.ja: しかし、それ以来、衰へたのは、劉の健康ばかりではない。劉の家産も亦とんとん拍子に傾いて、今では、三百畝を以て数へた負郭の田も、多くは人の手に渡つた。劉自身も、余儀なく、馴れない手に鋤を執つて、佗しいその日その日を送つてゐるのである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Since he spat out the wine worm, why did Liu's health fail? Why did his fortune decline — once the spitting of the wine worm and Liu's later ruin are set side by side as cause and effect, this is a question that readily occurs to anyone. Indeed this question has been repeated by people of every occupation living in Changshan, and from their mouths answers of every kind have been given. The three answers given here are in truth no more than the most representative chosen from among them.
student.ja: 酒虫を吐いて以来、何故、劉の健康が衰へたか。何故、家産が傾いたか――酒虫を吐いたと云ふ事と、劉のその後の零落とを、因果の関係に並べて見る以上、これは、誰にでも起りやすい疑問である。現にこの疑問は、長山に住んでゐる、あらゆる職業の人人によつて繰返され、且、それらの人人の口から、あらゆる種類の答を与へられた。今、ここに挙げる三つの答も、実はその中から、最、代表的なものを選んだのに過ぎない。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: The first answer. The wine worm was Liu's fortune, and not Liu's disease. By chancing to meet an ignorant barbarian monk, he willingly brought about the loss of this heaven-given fortune.
student.ja: 第一の答。酒虫は、劉の福であつて、劉の病ではない。偶、暗愚の蛮僧に遇つた為に、好んで、この天与の福を失ふやうな事になつたのである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: The second answer. The wine worm was Liu's disease, and not Liu's fortune. For to empty a whole jar at a single drinking is quite beyond what an ordinary man can conceive. Had the wine worm not been removed, Liu must undoubtedly have died before long. Seen in this light, poverty and sickness arriving each in turn should rather be called happiness for Liu.
student.ja: 第二の答。酒虫は、劉の病であつて、劉の福ではない。何故と云へば、一飲一甕を尽すなどと云ふ事は、到底、常人の考へられない所だからである。そこで、もし酒虫を除かなかつたなら、劉は必久しからずして、死んだのに相違ない。して見ると、貧病、迭に至るのも、寧劉にとつては、幸福と云ふべきである。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: The third answer. The wine worm was neither Liu's disease nor Liu's fortune. Liu from of old did nothing but drink. If wine were taken away from Liu's life, nothing would remain behind. Seen in this light, Liu is the wine worm, and the wine worm is Liu. Hence Liu's casting off the wine worm was the same as killing himself. That is to say, from the day he became unable to drink, Liu is Liu and yet is not Liu. If Liu himself were already gone, then it is entirely natural, and only to be expected, that the health and fortune of the Liu of former days should have been lost.
student.ja: 第三の答。酒虫は、劉の病でもなければ、劉の福でもない。劉は、昔から酒ばかり飲んでゐた。劉の一生から酒を除けば、後には、何も残らない。して見ると、劉は即酒虫、酒虫は即劉である。だから、劉が酒虫を去つたのは自ら己を殺したのも同前である。つまり、酒が飲めなくなつた日から、劉は劉にして、劉ではない。劉自身が既になくなつてゐたとしたら、昔日の劉の健康なり家産なりが、失はれたのも、至極、当然な話であらう。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: Which of these answers best hits the mark, I myself do not know. I have done no more than list such moral judgements at the end of this tale, in imitation of the *Didacticism* of the Chinese novelists.
student.ja: これらの答の中で、どれが、最よく、当を得てゐるか、それは自分にもわからない。自分は、唯、支那の小説家の Didacticism に倣つて、かう云ふ道徳的な判断を、この話の最後に、列挙して見たまでゝある。
student.label: house-checked

student.en: — Fourth month of the fifth year —
student.ja: ――五年四月――
student.label: house-checked
